findings.problem: println! side-effect hidden inside the mapping closure of load_metrics; I/O, parsing, allocation, and domain construction are fused into one function
findings.failure_mode: Caller cannot reason about side effects; pure consumers of Record cannot be composed; metrics loading leaks logging into the data pipeline making it impossible to suppress or redirect output without modifying core logic
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely. Split load_metrics into a pure parse_lines(input: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and a shell layer that handles fs::read_to_string, printing, and error rendering

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permissions, disk error)
findings.failure_mode: Entire process aborts with a panic instead of returning a typed error that a caller can handle, retry, or report gracefully
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value in the second CSV field
findings.failure_mode: Malformed input line causes process panic instead of returning a typed ParseError; an attacker or bad file can trigger denial of service
findings.fix: Use map_err to return a typed ParseError::InvalidValue and never unwrap on parse

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses the split result by index with no bounds check before use
findings.failure_mode: Empty or single-element line causes index-out-of-bounds panic; untrusted input crashes the process
findings.fix: Validate parts.len() >= 2 with an early return of a typed error (e.g., ParseError::Malformed) before any indexed access

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses the split result by index with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: Same as above; untrusted CSV with one field panics on the second indexed access
findings.fix: Same validation at line 16 gate; parts[1] is only reachable after len check

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast; values 65536-4294967295 silently truncate to u16 range
findings.failure_mode: Data integrity violation: large numeric values wrap silently, producing incorrect Record values with no error indication
findings.fix: Use u16::from_str_radix(value.trim(), 10).map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue) to parse directly as u16, eliminating the cast

findings.problem: load_metrics fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing (split/collect), side effects (println!), allocation (Vec<String> intermediate), and domain construction (Record) into a single function
findings.failure_mode: Violates Data/Calculations/Actions separation; impossible to unit-test pure parsing without mocking filesystem; impossible to suppress I/O in consumers; violates Parse-don't-validate (no trusted domain type guards)
findings.fix: Extract a pure parse_line(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> for calculations; shell load_metrics calls fs::read_to_string, splits into lines, maps each through parse_line, and collects errors

findings.problem: Collects split CSV parts into Vec<String> via collect() before accessing individual elements; allocates a Vec of String clones unnecessarily
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded heap allocation per line; every CSV row allocates a Vec plus N String allocations; no try_reserve, no domain cap on max_items
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Malformed) to get (_name, value_str) directly with zero intermediate Vec; parse value_str without collect

findings.problem: No domain error type exists; all failures collapse to panics via unwrap() throughout the function
findings.failure_mode: Caller has no way to distinguish I/O errors, malformed lines, invalid values, or capacity errors; recovery and observability are impossible
findings.fix: Define enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Malformed, InvalidValue, TooMany, Overflow }; return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> from load_metrics

no profiler evidence for allocation hot path

residual_risk: Static review only. The crate contains 9 BLOCKER violations including hidden I/O, 2 unwrap panics on external input, 2 unchecked index panics, a lossy cast, unbounded per-line allocation, shell leakage, and no error taxonomy. No commands were executed; functional verification requires cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo check, cargo test, and behavior tests. The code must be refactored into a pure parse layer with typed errors, file I/O in the shell, and the println! side effect removed.
